text: CSV, comma-separated values, is the universal format for spreadsheets and tabular data — and Python handles it natively.
The csv module writes rows safely, correctly handling commas and quotes inside your data.
You create a writer and hand it a list for each row — first a header, then the data.
[chuckle] It formats everything into proper CSV text, ready to save or open in any spreadsheet program.
[sniff] Reading is just as easy, and DictReader is the star — it turns each row into a dictionary.
It uses the header row as the keys, so you access columns by name instead of by fragile numeric position.
So you read row dot name and row dot score clearly, instead of guessing which column is which.
[sigh] That makes your data-processing code readable and robust, even if columns get reordered.
[groan] Whenever you deal with exported data or reports, the csv module is the reliable, correct way to read and write it.
